equivalent.core/sched/scheduler.go:getNextBatchToRu: the last extend batch was formed by the previous call of getNewBatchPrefill, which ends by storing s.chunkedReq into that batch's ChunkedReq, and nothing assigns s.chunkedReq between two calls; so when last.ChunkedReq is not nil it is s.chunkedReq, which getNextBatchToRun has just put in exclude, and when it is nil exclude[nil] filters no request: with the test flipped the same set of requests is excluded

the guard is always true when a chunked request exists, so > and >= take the same branch: a chunked request's ExtendEnd is set by the previous pass, by commit (extend > 0) or by addChunkedReq (PrefixLen plus min(remaining prompt, chunk budget), and the budget is at least one token: the running requests mixed in and the shorter requests admitted before the chunk each take a token of the chunk size, and the chunk was admitted only because one was left), and the stash that follows sets PrefixLen to ExtendEnd only after this test; a 28000-scenario search with tiny chunk sizes under mixed chunking and shortest-prefill-first never reached ExtendEnd == PrefixLen

releasing no pages stages an empty list under needSort, which only makes the merge run once more over a free list that is already sorted, and prepends nothing otherwise

the branch is entered only when the ranks or the ratios differ; if the ranks are equal the ratios differ, so ki.ratio <= kj.ratio and ki.ratio < kj.ratio agree, and if the ranks differ the equality test before it is false (a ratio is never NaN here: the divisor uncached is positive)

equivalent.lower/lower.go:CaptureBatchSizes:>->>=#1: when largest equals numMax the mutant appends numMax to a capture list that already holds that value (largest is an element of it); the next loop drops repeated sizes through the seen set and the result is sorted, so the returned sizes are the same either way.

equivalent.core/cache/full.go:releaseLock:==->!=#1:: releaseLock has one caller, treeCore.DecLockRef, which calls updateLeaves on the released node right after it returns, so the node's own call here is redundant. For the ancestors reached, every node in the tree other than the root holds a non-nil device value (nodes are created with one and eviction deletes them from the tree: there is no host tier, so no tombstone), so an ancestor of a locked node always has a child with a value and is never a device leaf; updateLeaves(ancestor) with lockRef 0 only deletes an entry that is not in leaves. With lockRef above 0 (the mutant's branch) isDeviceLeaf is false and updateLeaves deletes an entry that acquireLock already removed and no path re-adds while locked. So leaves, evictable and protected are identical after either version.

With Decode Graph the first case matches and the other cases also accept every Other; with Decode Eager the case 'Decode == Eager && Other == Eager' accepts Other Eager, and 'Decode == Graph || Other == Eager' adds only Other Eager, so the set of accepted pairs is the same.
